source.title: The Role of Fine-grained Harm Signals in LLM Safety
source.authors: Soyeon Park; Seogyeong Jeong; Sunwoo Kim; Alice Oh

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests steering with category-specific difference-in-means residuals, rather than ablating or adding the pooled refusal direction. It measures effects on harmfulness attribution and refusal, providing a conceptual test of category-specific contributions.
record.gate_note: The paper constructs harmfulness directions from harmful-minus-matched-harmless mean activations, then removes their component along the pooled general-harm direction. It adds category residuals, not the pooled general-harm direction. Figure-only results are recorded as such. Values used to choose steering strengths are not separate results. The second prompt-set robustness comparison is shown in a figure without extractable values and is not separately rowed.
record.test_reason: The study steers category-specific difference-in-means residuals, made orthogonal to a pooled harmful-minus-harmless direction, and measures induced refusal on benign prompts and shifts in harm judgments. That bears on whether directions beyond the pooled one drive refusal (V4) and whether harm judgment and refusal come apart (V5). It never ablates or adds the pooled direction itself, so V1 is not tested. The pooled vector is taken at the final user-instruction token, Zhao et al.'s harmfulness position, not Arditi's post-instruction refusal position.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that category residuals can encode harmfulness, with a category pattern that holds across models, and can induce refusal, with a more model-dependent pattern. Though orthogonal to general harm at the intervention layer, they amplify downstream general-harm representations. So fine-grained harm signals matter beyond the shared general-harm direction. They do not claim the single refusal direction is wrong.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless mean differences at the final user-instruction token, but constructs category-specific directions after projecting out the pooled general-harm direction. It steers these residuals rather than ablating the pooled direction; no addition of the pooled direction or capability-retention test is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: Category and model change refusal effects; α differs by model (0.25 for Gemma and Llama, 0.6 for Qwen). The authors report that Qwen showed little change at α=0.25. A disjoint second set of 100 prompts is used for robustness, with results shown graphically.

fits_no_version.finding: Category residuals, orthogonal to general harm at the injection layer, raise downstream cosine alignment with the general-harm vector above random orthogonal controls. The rise is strongest at beta 0.6 and in middle-to-late layers (Figs. 3-5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directions orthogonal to the harm/refusal direction at one layer can amplify it in later layers.

record.problems: Only three similarly sized instruction-tuned models and one harm taxonomy are tested. Directions are extracted at the final user-instruction token. Refusal is identified by fixed substrings, and the authors note that the classifier and task formats may not fully capture refusal. Absolute effect sizes across models are not directly comparable because steering strengths differ. Many plotted values are not numerically stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, harmfulness-attribution results for the remaining three Llama categories (tailored financial advice, economic harm, fraud and deception), the remaining three Qwen categories (tailored financial advice, economic harm, fraud and deception), and the remaining Gemma categories (tailored financial advice, economic harm, fraud and deception) are omitted; the plotted results are in Figure 2, left. Downstream general-harm alignment curves (Figures 3–5) and the second-sample robustness plots (Figure 6) are also not separately rowed; they report cosine-alignment outcomes rather than refusal or harmfulness judgments named by the tested versions. No numeric values for those plots are stated in the text.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the pooled difference-in-means direction, and no capability-retention check.
No comparison of affine, cone or dominant-plus-others models, and no ablation of residuals to test whether they are needed for refusal.
No probing of separate internal encodings. The evidence is behavioural, from steering residual directions only.

missing.what: Within-model rank correlation between harm attribution and induced refusal: rho 0.94 (Gemma), 0.81 (Llama), 0.82 (Qwen)
Cross-model rank correlations of induced refusal: rho 0.80, 0.75, 0.59 (Gemma-Llama, Gemma-Qwen, Llama-Qwen)
Qwen showed little change at alpha 0.25, so alpha 0.6 was needed

record.verdict_notes: V1 labels removed: the study never manipulates the pooled direction. The reader's V5 'limits_scope' about not probing encodings was an untested part, and is replaced by the rank-correlation limitation. Most values are figure-only. Refusal is classified by substrings.

versions.untested_parts: Tests addition of category residuals and measures induced refusal; does not add the pooled general-harm difference-in-means direction, ablate a direction, test removal across every layer and position, or assess preservation of general capabilities.
No jailbreak suppression experiment or training against ablation.
Tests category residuals as multiple fine-grained components; does not compare affine, cone, or dominant-direction-plus-others models of refusal.
Compares harmfulness attribution and refusal responses under category-residual steering, but does not directly establish separate internal encodings or probe a refusal decision representation.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.

relationships.condition: Category residuals orthogonal to the pooled harm direction at the intervention layer, added at instruction and template tokens, in Gemma-2-9B, Llama-3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B
relationships.reason: The text says the residuals turn benign non-refusals into refusals. Qwen gives nonzero rates of 1.0% and 7.1% (R23, R27), and adult content gives the highest rate in Gemma and Qwen (R02, R24).
relationships.display_finding: Orthogonal category residuals induced refusal on previously accepted benign prompts, including Qwen rates of 1.0% and 7.1%, with adult content highest in Gemma and Qwen.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Category residuals orthogonal to the pooled harm direction at the intervention layer, added at instruction and template tokens, in Gemma-2-9B, Llama-3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B
source_check.reason: The cited rows are only partial (1.0%, 7.1%) or figure-only (R02, R24). The pooled vector is a harm direction taken at the final instruction token, not a refusal direction, and it is never steered for comparison. Sec. 3.3 shows the residuals raise downstream general-harm alignment, so refusal may run through the pooled direction. That qualifies V4's 'other directions' rather than supporting them. Steering is also applied at every layer, not one intervention layer.

relationships.condition: Across models, categories and the downstream mechanism
relationships.reason: Refusal induction is uneven: as low as 1.0% (R23), cross-model ranks only rho 0.59-0.80, adult content fifth in Llama (R13). Qwen needed alpha 0.6. Sec. 3.3 shows the residuals raise downstream general-harm alignment, so they may act through the pooled direction in later layers.
relationships.display_finding: Refusal induction was as low as 1.0%, cross-model rank correlations were 0.59–0.80, adult content ranked fifth in Llama, and Qwen required α=0.6; residual signals increased downstream general-harm alignment and may act through the pooled direction in later layers.

The study never extracts a refusal direction, never steers the pooled vector, and never ablates anything. The random control is only in Sec. 3.3, no uncertainty is reported, and refusal is judged by substrings. R02/R13/R24 still link V1, which R23/R27 dropped.
